summary: Dynamic ingress policy shift causing persistent 429s for parallel ingest
description: Issue summary: Customer reports an increase in persistent 429s for a sustained parallel ingest job immediately after a dynamic ingress policy change that split traffic across two rate-shard groups. Impact: BrightDesk's nightly indexer (100 concurrent workers) received ~40-60% 429s for ~3 hours, causing a delayed processing window and missed SLA for that job. Environment: Dedicated pool, prod us-west, policy change rolled at 2026-03-13T02:12Z. Steps to reproduce: 1) Configure 100 parallel connections to /v1/embeddings with their API key. 2) Trigger concurrent batch (multipart) upload using the customer's backfill script. 3) Observe early 429s within first 30s that remain sticky. Observed behavior: 429s include X-RateLimit-Reason: token-window-exhausted and X-RateLimit-Window: 1s; headers show per-route counters diverging. Expected behavior: after ingress split, token accounting should preserve tenant-level refill equivalence and not create persistent imbalances. Logs/Dashboards: request traces: https://dashboards.redwood.com/s/ingress/throttle_heatmap?org=brightdesk, sample trace: trace-id 0f3a1c7e (link redwood-traces), gateway logs: s3://redwood-logs/brightdesk/2026-03-13/gateway.log
comments: 2026-03-13 03:04 - Support (Aisha): Opened ticket, requested customer to provide sample cURL and a timestamped log when 429s occurred.
2026-03-13 03:22 - Customer (BrightDesk-ops): Provided backfill script, sample timeframe 02:15-05:10 UTC, attached local worker logs (attached to ticket).
2026-03-13 05:18 - SRE (Miguel): Observed sudden split of ingress weight from single shard -> two shards at 02:12Z; refill counters did not copy across during policy commit. Added to investigation.

2026-03-13 08:40 - Support (Aisha): Temporary mitigation recommended: stagger worker start times by 10s and reduce concurrency to 60 while we investigate. Customer moved to 'Waiting on Support' to apply mitigation.

2026-03-14 02:12 - SRE (Miguel): Hotfix deployed to backfill token buckets and align refill rates across new shards (rolled to canary then global). Noted in-channel: #support, #sre-ingress (slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C03SRE123/p1678783).
investigation_notes: Ingress policy change at 2026-03-13T02:12Z split tenant BrightDesk traffic to two logical shards to balance load across a new edge cluster.
Rate-limiter maintains per-shard token windows; migration code assumed zero-diff but left original shard counters at near-zero and new shard at full refill, creating asymmetric consumption.

During parallel worker fanout, some connections hit the depleted shard repeatedly due to connection affinity (keepalive pooled to subset of proxies), generating sticky 429s despite tenant quota being available overall.
Headers observed: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 on some connections while other connections for same key showed Remaining: 1200. Token refill timestamp mismatch (delta ~45s) between shards.
Hypothesis: connection affinity + shard counter drift + small refill window (1s) created microbursts that the client's retry logic couldn't smooth out, causing aggregated 429 rate to remain high.
Related systems reviewed: ingress rollout logs, proxy connection pools, token-migration script (PR #1782).
resolution: Hotfix applied 2026-03-14 02:10Z: migration job updated to copy remaining token allowances from source shard to target shards and to atomically flip shard routing. Rollout notes: canary 02:02Z -> full at 02:10Z.
Applied short-term customer workaround: increased tenant burst allowance by +30% for BrightDesk until midnight UTC and recommended staggered worker restarts.
Post-fix validation: heatmap and request traces show 429 rate dropped from 48% -> <2% for the job window. Confirmed with customer at 2026-03-14 04:30Z.

Follow-ups: patch ingress control-plane to include a guarded migration step (stage token backfill then do routing flip) and add console warning for policy splits that will touch active tenants. Created internal task INT-902345 to implement permanent fix.
